thread:
jess: Hey support - running batch rerank via CSV import and seeing per-query candidate counts mismatch. One query returns 5 scores but only 3 candidates. API responds 200 and a successful job id, but output arrays are misaligned :frowning:
ara: Ugh. Can you share the exact request (or a minimal repro) and the job id?
jess: job_id=job_2026_03_12_42, using the UI CSV uploader. Quick excerpt of CSV (columns: query, candidates):
```
query,candidates
How to cook rice,"rice cooker|boil|microwave"
Best cloud GPUs,"a100|v100|t4"
Top rerank tips,"tokenization|batching"
Multi query test,"one||three"  <-- notice the empty middle candidate
```
jess: Attached the output JSON we got back (redacted):
```
{ "queries": [ {"q":"...","candidates":["...","...","..."],"scores":[0.98,0.76,0.63,0.20,0.05] }, ... ] }
```
jess: So scores length > candidates length for that entry. Not truncating, just extra trailing scores.
ara: Did you upload via UI or hit the REST endpoint directly? Sometimes the UI trims trailing empty CSV fields weirdly. Also which delimiter did you use?
jess: UI -> advanced -> CSV delimiter is pipe (|). We used pipes inside the candidates field and also the CSV was exported from a spreadsheet so some rows ended up with double pipes for an empty candidate.
ara: Ok that double-pipe could be the source. The server's CSV parser currently collapses consecutive delimiters to empty strings in candidates list, but downstream code filters empty strings only in the UI path, not the batch engine. That mismatch could produce empty candidate entries that later get dropped or produce extra score slots.
mike: Looping in eng-runtime. @eng-runtime can you look at job_2026_03_12_42 logs? We might be normalizing candidates twice.
eng-runtime: Got it — pulling logs. I see at parse stage: 
```
INFO parse_csv_row row=123 candidates_raw="one||three" -> split -> ["one","","three"]
WARN normalize_candidates filtered 1 empty -> ["one","three"] but score_mapping kept original indices -> scores_len=3 vs exported_scores_len=5
```
eng-runtime: So there's a bug where score assignment indexes are computed before filtering empties, leading to padding mismatch. Repro steps: 1) CSV row with consecutive delimiters (empty candidate) 2) system splits -> empty token 3) normalization step removes empty entries 4) scoring map still refers to original slots -> out-of-sync arrays.
ara: Thanks. Severity? Customer-facing wrong outputs -> high.
mike: Quick mitigation: when normalization removes entries, we should also remove corresponding score slots or emit a 400 if scores provided count != candidates post-normalization. For existing jobs we should add a cleanup that reconciles arrays and mark as "recalculated" so results are correct.
eng-runtime: I'll push a hotfix: 1) treat consecutive delimiters as explicit empty candidate and preserve them (UI behavior) OR 2) enforce rejection with clear error. Prefer (1) for backwards compatibility. Implementing immediate reconciliation for in-flight jobs and adding a server-side validation check so future runs return 400 with error_code=ERR_CANDIDATE_COUNT_MISMATCH.
jess: Appreciate the triage. Any ETA? Customer is blocked on a pilot.
mike: Hotfix branch created, PR incoming. If reviews go quick we can deploy a patch to staging in ~2h and prod in ~6h (rolling).
support-bot: Ticket created: #SUP-1428 (batch-rerank csv empty-candidate mismatch). Assigned to eng-runtime.
ara: For the customer workaround: ask them to replace double pipes with a placeholder like "(empty)" or to export CSV with quoted empty fields so parser preserves empties. Also include a sample curl repro in case they prefer the REST path.
jess: Sending repro and temporary CSV fix. Will update customer. Thanks all :thumbsup:
